value.rationale: A natural combinatorial-polytope graph-distance problem: bounded in-degree is used to make causal-discovery polytopes tractable, and the four-node bound-two face is its first proper nontrivial example. The complete sharp graph metric and self-centered yet nonregular behavior are neither routine counts of faces nor obvious consequences of the H-representation; the invariant is directly relevant to possible edge-walk lengths. It is intentionally finite and does not assert algorithmic complexity improvements.
